summary: RECOMMENDATION: "Frozen Foods" should NOT exist as a category and should be deprecated. "Frozen" describes how an item is stored, not what it is, and the catalog already tracks that orthogonally via defaultStorage and a per-storage freshnessByStorage range. The established convention is already in place and well-followed: frozen-stored staples live in their semantic category with defaultStorage=Frozen and a Frozen freshness range (e.g. corn/spinach/blueberry/strawberry are Produce with Frozen ranges; shrimp/prawn/salmon/tuna/meatball are Protein with defaultStorage=Frozen; waffle/pie shell/dumpling wrapper are Breads & Bakery with defaultStorage=Frozen; pizza dough is Breads & Bakery). Existing items even fold the frozen form into aliases of the fresh item (corn has 'frozen corn'/'frozen sweet corn', spinach has 'frozen spinach', shrimp has 'frozen shrimp'). Across 2277 items, 69 already use defaultStorage=Frozen and only ONE of them sits in 'Frozen Foods' (ice cream) — it is an orphan category of one. A user adding 'frozen peas' should match the Produce 'pea' item (storage Frozen), not a separate Frozen Foods bucket; a single 'Frozen Foods' category would otherwise fragment matching and duplicate every freezable food. Concrete action: (1) move the lone item 'ice cream' to 'Dairy & Eggs' (it carries allergens:[dairy]) or 'Snacks', (2) retire the 'Frozen Foods' category string, (3) keep classifying all frozen staples by what they are with defaultStorage=Frozen. Consequently, every staple the brief lists below is annotated as 'belongs in <category> with Frozen storage' rather than proposed for a Frozen category. Freshness ranges below follow the catalog's existing frozen conventions (frozen veg/fruit ~180-365d; pastry/dough ~90-180d) and are corroborated by USDA FoodKeeper / FSIS guidance (frozen veg best quality 8-12 months; frozen puff pastry 6-12 months).
issues: 'Frozen Foods' is a storage-defined category, which collides conceptually with the orthogonal defaultStorage/freshnessByStorage fields the schema already uses to model freezing. This is the only category named after a storage state rather than a food type.

The category holds exactly 1 item (ice cream) while 68 other Frozen-storage items are correctly classified by food type in Produce/Protein/Breads & Bakery/Pasta & Noodles/etc. This is an inconsistency, not a populated category.

The sole item 'ice cream' is mis-categorized regardless: it has allergens:[dairy] and dietaryTags Vegetarian/Gluten-Free/Nut-Free, so it belongs in 'Dairy & Eggs' (or 'Snacks'), not in a storage bucket.

Several genuinely frozen-only staples named in the brief are simply absent from the catalog entirely (edamame, frozen french fries, hash browns, gyoza/potsticker, frozen herb cubes, pizza base/crust, frozen mixed vegetables, sorbet). These are real gaps but should be filled inside their food-type categories, not a Frozen category.

'ice cream' freshnessByStorage only declares a Frozen range [60,180]; that is acceptable since ice cream is frozen-only, but it lacks Refrigerated/Pantry which is correct here — flag only that this is the lone single-storage item to keep if the category is dissolved.

cleanups.fix: Move out of category 'Frozen Foods' into 'Dairy & Eggs' (it has allergens:[dairy]) or 'Snacks'. Keep defaultStorage=Frozen and freshnessByStorage.Frozen=[60,180]. This empties and lets you retire the 'Frozen Foods' category string.

Deprecate/remove the 'Frozen Foods' category entirely once ice-cream is re-homed. Frozen-ness is already modeled by defaultStorage='Frozen' + freshnessByStorage['Frozen']; a storage-named category duplicates that and fragments item matching.
